# Offline Capacity Harness And Transport Decisions

This contributor tool implements capacity-harness simulations and conditional
transport decision records. It is not an installed SDK feature, a load generator
for real Docker, or a capacity certification. Every report is labeled
`simulation: true` and `qualification: unqualified`, including successful runs.
The existing CLI, Compose and Buildx routes and the simulated overhead benchmark
are unchanged.

## Run A Simulation

From the checkout root, using the installed locked development environment:

```bash
uv run --offline --locked python -m scripts.fleet_harness --help
uv run --offline --locked python -m scripts.fleet_harness run \
  --manifest scripts/fleet_harness/fixtures/manifest.json \
  --input scripts/fleet_harness/fixtures/plan.json > simulation.json
uv run --offline --locked python -m scripts.fleet_harness schema --kind plan
uv run --offline --locked python -m scripts.fleet_harness schema --kind manifest
```

The fictional example simulates creation, inventory and a separately authorized
recovery fault. It creates no processes, sockets, containers or host resources.
The only provider is the built-in in-memory fake. Setting `provider` to `real`
returns a rejected report and zero provider calls; it does not contact an endpoint.
No arbitrary adapter imports, endpoint URIs, provisioners or prune operations exist.

`--manifest` uses the strict fleet contributor contract, with all draft decisions
resolved. Runnable configuration is not permission to execute. Before constructing
the fake, the harness requires `opt_in: true`, declared disposable isolation
evidence, endpoint/action allowlists, an ownership namespace and marker, finite
stop limits, explicit artifact access/retention, and an owned-resource teardown
plan. Every step's effective endpoint and action must be allowed, and every fault
must name its individually authorized scenario. One authorized fault does not
authorize another. These are operator **declarations, not security authentication**;
neither references, tags nor aliases establish authority or actual isolation.

## Plans, Limits And Ownership

A plan contains explicit steps and repetitions, a `maximum_samples` memory bound,
a finite per-operation deadline, scripted metric observations, and simulated
cleanup durations/failures. Steps name a scenario, endpoint alias and action.
Creation, pull and build steps allocate their named removable asset slot;
start/stop/remove require an already acquired identity. Slots must be declared
created, ephemeral and `remove_owned`. Borrowed, persistent and retained assets
are never cleanup targets. Resource IDs are generated by the fake, not accepted
as deletion targets from input. Several aliases for one effective endpoint share
the same identity scope.

The fake clock bounds queueing, local work, readiness and recovery by both the
operation deadline and remaining run budget. Exhausting queue time launches no
command. A timeout after simulated creation retains the acquired identity in the
ledger; it is not evidence of rollback or safe retry. Load stops on declared time,
failure fraction, unknown count, created-asset or resource early-stop limits.
Unavailable budgeted resource observations stop load rather than pretending the
limit was enforced. A short script is reported as `plan_exhausted` unless it
reaches the manifest's duration or operation-submission termination threshold.

Cleanup has its own finite budget. It visits only exact acquired live identities
in reverse order, scoped by effective endpoint, kind, ID, namespace and marker.
Failed or timed-out cleanup remains visible as exact residual identities and a
`cleanup_residual` reason. No daemon-wide discovery/deletion is performed. Fake
clock bounds do **not** qualify a real blocking adapter's deadline behavior.

## Read The Report

JSON goes to stdout, so an operator chooses the destination file and applies the
declared access/retention policy. The tool does not enforce filesystem permissions
or delete expired reports. Exit 0 means an artifact was produced, not passing
criteria: inspect `status`, `reasons`, `outcomes` and `cleanup`. Invalid input and
authorization/provider rejection exit 2; validation failures include a zero-call
receipt and sanitized error codes. Unknown input keys, file paths and validator
messages are not echoed in errors.

All submitted terminal outcomes, including failures, cancellations, unknowns and
timeouts, remain in the denominator. Queue observations cover every submission;
local observations cover launches; readiness and fault recovery retain their own
boundaries. Timings carry fake-clock start/end seconds. Distributions use nearest
rank across all observed outcome timings, not successes only. Unavailable seconds
and resource high-water values are `null`, never silently zero-filled. The report
includes command counts, CPU, RSS, file descriptors, children, disk bytes/inodes,
network and daemon observations; omitted metrics are explicitly unavailable.

`load_elapsed_seconds` excludes cleanup; `elapsed_seconds` includes it. Metrics
are scripted high-waters sampled after each simulated submission, not OS counters.
Interpreter/library versions are local observations; Docker/plugin/kernel/host
versions remain explicitly unavailable. Hardware, topology, workload mix, images
and cache state are labeled declarations, not measured target metadata. Private
connection references are withheld. No credentials, argv, application output or
raw exception fields are collected. This is not a secret scanner: use synthetic
data and safe aliases in all free-text fields and metadata.

## Conditional Transport Decision

```bash
uv run --offline --locked python -m scripts.fleet_harness decide \
  --input scripts/fleet_harness/fixtures/no-baseline.json > decision.json
uv run --offline --locked python -m scripts.fleet_harness schema --kind experiment
```

Without a representative real material-overhead baseline against a declared
operator objective, the result is `no_go`, with zero candidate launches and zero
connections. Even a supplied baseline claiming independent review cannot enable
a real trial: the real binding/deadline adapter is unqualified. Baseline references
are declarations, not authenticated evidence.

An optional `comparison` accepts two prerecorded harness reports (`cli` and
`candidate`) and explicit `cli_contract`/`candidate_contract` records. It compares
workload/operation inputs, repetitions, environment/cache state and completion,
plus authentication, endpoint verification, API versions, errors, permissions,
result shapes, ordering, backpressure, byte accounting, ownership, early close,
cancellation, timeout, confidentiality and ambiguous mutation semantics. Any
mismatch rejects the comparison even if candidate timings improve. Both reports,
including failed/unavailable samples, distributions and teardown, remain in the
decision artifact. Equal simulations yield only `matched_simulation`, never a go
or production-adoption recommendation. This tool performs no statistical inference
or confidence claim from fictional timings. The selected route remains `cli` and
Compose/Buildx remain unchanged.

Real capacity qualification and a measured transport trial are **blocked** until
an independently qualified endpoint-binding/deadline adapter and separately
authorized disposable infrastructure are provided, with verified versions,
representative workloads, materiality criteria, measured observations and
independent owned-resource teardown read-back. Do not use workstation Docker,
host CI provisioning, shared-host pruning or these fictional thresholds as a
substitute. No portable fleet size or capacity envelope is established here.
